# Gina Rooks — "Preliminary notes" — 2026-09-11

The practitioner feedback email behind Phase 21, reproduced in full and verbatim.

- From: Gina Rooks <ginarooksnp@gmail.com>
- To: Sam Shamber <sshamber01@gmail.com>, Lauren Perkins <ventures@designthefuture.studio>
- Date: 2026-09-11 15:00 ET (19:00 UTC)
- Subject: Preliminary notes

Five inline screenshots were attached; they are marked `[image: image.png]` below,
at the points where they appeared. They show, in order: the favorites list, Strive's
clinical difference statements, the Review & Send screen, and two LifeFile
prescription-entry windows.

This file is a primary source for Phase 21 work orders. It is committed read-only:
never edit it, never summarise it in place. Quote it. Every work order that claims

---

I had a little time to look over more, here are some preliminary notes.

For injectable medications it would be helpful to have the mg dosing as well when it shows up under favorites - it could say 10 units (0.5 mg) next to injectable solution.

[image: image.png]

I noticed the Rx's are missing a few things:
1) Duration (30 days, 90 days, etc.).
2) Quantity/count for how many to dispense at a time.
3) Injectable vials come in various sizes so you also need to select vial size and cost varies based on that. Having some kind of calculation built in to help auto select vial size based on inputted Rx would be nice.
4) How many refills are authorized.

5) Drugs like GLP1s also need clinical difference statements (patient-specific reason for compound versus commercial product) so will need a spot for that - for example, Glycine added to help maintain muscle mass. These are some that Strive uses:
[image: image.png]

6) Injectable meds will need to include Rx for syringes if needed or indicate no syringes if patient gets elsewhere.
7) Shipping type - temp sensitive shipping or not.
8) Allergies or no known drug allergies is needed on the Rx.
9) Place to add diagnosis which isn't always needed but should be there for certain Rx.
10) A place to add special instructions for instance removing a filler, dyes, etc.

I don't see a way to go back and edit an Rx when you are at review and send, just a remove button. Clicking back didn't work either, is there a way that I am missing? Or a pending Rx queue?
[image: image.png]

I did try saving one as a draft and I can't then edit it as far as I can see, so that would need to be added as well as the ability to add other Rx to that order and sign all at once.

I also wondered about shipping costs. I don't see it listed anywhere with the med pricing or when you get to review and sign. That is another downside to ordering from more than one clinic for one patient. You might get better pricing but you then you pay shipping more than once, so would want that built in as well.

On the favorites, when selected, it would be nice to still be able to revert to the Rx builder drop downs rather than editing a free text box. Or to have below the saved version, options for frequently used other doses. It's would be kind of busy to save every single unit dose of semaglutide or testosterone in the favorite list. I'd prefer to see semaglutide injection, click it and see the most common prescription doses written out to select or then be able to add a custom one. Also for favorites, it would be nice to see sorted alphabetically and/or by category as the list could get long. Also a frequently used section would be nice with the ability to then convert it to a favorite.

Here are 2 windows to show how the lifefile system handles prescription entry for reference.
[image: image.png]
[image: image.png]

*Gina Rooks, MSN, APRN, FNP-C, CFNIP*

## What this email does and does not cover

Covers, as numbered items 1–10 plus the closing paragraphs: duration, dispense
quantity, vial size with a suggestion calculation, refills, clinical difference
statements, syringes, shipping type, allergies, diagnosis, special instructions,
editing an Rx at Review, editing a draft and signing several at once, shipping cost
shown in pricing and charged once, and the favorites asks (builder dropdowns rather
than a free-text box, common doses per medication, sorting, a frequently-used
section).

Does not cover: titration, taper, ramp-up, dose escalation, or any schedule that
changes over time. Those words do not appear. The titration request (WO-105) comes
from the 2026-09-11 Product Run Thru meeting — see
[2026-09-11-product-run-thru-transcript.md](2026-09-11-product-run-thru-transcript.md).
